Structure

This page proposes how the claim tagger MVP sits in Notion: five tables, four views and three sub-pages, all under the page "Feedback Distillation MVP". Nothing else is built in Notion until it is approved.

To approve, say go as it stands, or edit this page first and then say go; the build follows the page as you leave it.

Sample rows use real claims from the audit of 9 October, with claims and ids shortened; the values in them are illustrations, not results.

At a glance

TableRows at setupWho writes to it
Rulebook copy13, one per tagSetup copies the rows once; the team may edit by hand; the agent writes only When to use, after a safety check PASS
Claims copy50 claimsSetup copies the rows once; the agent writes only Agent tags and Agent notes
Tag decisions (the queue)10, the audit's decisions, already decidedThe agent adds a row for every unsure answer; the editor decides it
Rule changesnoneThe agent proposes changes to rules; the editor approves or rejects them
Agent settings1A person ticks Paused; the agent writes Rulebook edition and Last run summary

Sub-pages:

  • Structure proposal: this page; it stays as history after approval.
  • Demos: one practice page per walkthrough run, each with its own small tables and the same four view names; never deleted.
  • Demo tests: the walkthrough skill's own test runs.

Rulebook copy

The 13 rows of the taxonomy table "Claim Tags — verified" whose Work tags contain Issue, with the same column names and types: Context-dependent, Exact duplicate, Factually challenged, Improper capitalization, Improperly sourced, Incorrect grammar, Multi-sentence, Poor wording, Semantically duplicated, Source inaccessible, Trailing period, Unsourced, Wordy. Only Context-dependent is judged in the MVP; the other twelve rows are there so the rulebook is complete and the next tag is a switch, not a rebuild.

Who fills what: setup copies the 13 rows once; the team may edit any column by hand; the agent writes exactly one column, When to use, and only after a safety check PASS or a confirmed restore to an earlier edition. A hand edit to the When to use of a tag that has rules stops every command until the text is put back.

Geo Tag IDtextsetup, then the teamThe tag's id in Geo.
Polarityselectsetup, then the teamKept as in the taxonomy; the agent does not use it. Values: Classification, Positive, Issue
Statusselectsetup, then the teamWhether the tag is verified. Values: Verified, Proposed
Verified ondatesetup, then the teamWhen the tag was verified.
When to usetextsetup, then the team; the agent only after a safety check PASS or a confirmed restoreThe numbered rules the agent applies; a tag is judged only when this holds rules.
Work tagsmulti-selectsetup, then the teamThe work the tag belongs to; every row here has Issue. Values: Pipeline benchmark check, Issue
Createdcreated timeNotionWhen the row was made.
Created bycreated byNotionWho made the row.

Left out on purpose: the taxonomy's two relation columns to the claims tables; a relation must point at a table, and the real tables are protected.

Claims copy

50 claims copied once from the real table "U.S. Politics debate claims": the 10 claims with Context-dependent decisions in the audit of 9 October, plus 40 picked at random (the pick is recorded).

Who fills what: setup copies the rows once, Geo columns only; the agent writes Agent tags and Agent notes and nothing else; the real table is never written.

Geo NametitlesetupThe claim text.
Geo IDtextsetupThe claim's identity in Geo; the queue's Key starts with it.
Geo URLlinksetupThe claim's page in Geo.
Geo SourcestextsetupThe claim's sources, as Geo lists them.
Geo Tagsmulti-selectsetupThe claim's tags in Geo. Values: Debate, Democracy & Media, Economy, Featured, Immigration, Main claim, Politics, debate claim
Geo TopicstextsetupThe claim's topics in Geo.

Geo Name sourceselectsetupWhich space the claim's name was taken from. Values: This space, Other space (fallback)

Agent notestextthe agentAt most two short lines: line 1 the tags that apply or "no tags"; line 2 how many tags wait for an editor, what was not checked, and the rulebook edition, joined with " · ".

Tag decisions (the queue)

One row for every answer the agent is unsure about: it answered Can't tell, its readings disagreed, or its probability that the tag applies lies between 0.25 and 0.75. Confident answers get no row.

Who fills what: the agent writes the first nine columns; the editor writes the last three, and the agent never does, with one exception: at setup the ten audit decisions are seeded as decided rows, their Your reasoning starting "From the audit of 9 October:".

Columns

ColumnTypeWho fills itMeaning
Claimtitlethe agentThe claim text.
Keytextthe agentThe claim's Geo ID, two colons, the tag; one row per claim and tag.
Tagselectthe agentThe tag the row is about. Values: the 13 tag names of the Rulebook copy
Agent proposalselectthe agentThe agent's answer. Values: Applies, Does not apply, Can't tell
Agent confidencenumberthe agentHow sure the agent is of its answer, from 0.5 (a coin flip) to 1 (certain); the queue is sorted by it, lowest first.
Agent reasontextthe agentAt most 40 words, then the rule cited and how many runs agreed.
Claim linklinkthe agentLink to the claim's row in the Claims copy.
Rulebook editiontextthe agentThe edition the proposal was made under.
Follow-upselectthe agentSet after a safety check PASS, on the rows the change rests on. Values: Fixed, Still wrong
Tag outcomeselectthe editorThe editor's decision; empty means the row waits. Values: Applies, Does not apply
Why wrongselectthe editorThe editor's reason the agent was wrong. Values: Agent slip, Rule unclear, Rule should change
Your reasoningtextthe editorThe editor's words; "rule 4" typed here names the rule.

Rule changes

One row per proposed change to one rule.

Who fills what: the agent creates a row with Status Proposed; the editor approves or rejects it, optionally with Editor wording; after a safety check PASS the agent sets Live and writes the new text into the Rulebook copy; a rollback sets Rolled back and restores the earlier text.

Columns

ColumnTypeWho fills itMeaning
Lessontitlethe agentA short name for the change.
Tagselectthe agentThe tag the change is about. Values: the 13 tag names of the Rulebook copy
Ruletextthe agentWhich rule, for example "Context-dependent rule 3".
Kindselectthe agentWhat kind of change. Values: Clarify wording, Change the rule, Initial rules
Current texttextthe agentThe rule's text now.
Proposed texttextthe agentThe text the agent proposes.
Safety check resulttextthe agentFor example "PASS: examples 11/11, earlier 10/10, yours 2/2" or "FAIL: 'Excluding CNN from Air Force One violates the federal court order' now Does not apply".
Supporting rowstextthe agentOne line per decided row the change rests on: the claim shortened, " · ", the row's Key.
Editor wordingtextthe editorThe rule as the editor words it; when filled, the safety check tests it instead of the Proposed text. Never written by the agent.
Statusselectthe editor and the agentThe editor sets Approved and Rejected; the agent sets Proposed, Live and Rolled back. Values: Proposed, Approved, Rejected, Live, Rolled back

One change at three moments. It rests on the two waiting rows above, once the editor has decided them (Does not apply, Rule unclear, a note on rule 4).

Current textTest: could a reader who sees only this sentence say which specific thing each definite reference points at? If any answer is no, tag Context-dependent.
Proposed textTest: … points at? A reference that reads as general needs no answer. If any other answer is no, tag Context-dependent.

Column1. Proposed2. Approved, then FAIL3. Editor wording added, then PASS
Safety check resultemptyFAIL: 'Excluding CNN from Air Force One violates the federal court order' now Does not applyPASS: examples 11/11, earlier 10/10, yours 2/2
Editor wordingemptyemptyTest: … points at? A general reference ("the larger public health problem") needs no answer; an unnamed order or event ("the federal court order") does. …

After the FAIL nothing in the rulebook changed, and the report proposed one sentence for Editor wording. After the PASS the editor's wording is rule 4 in the Rulebook copy, the edition goes to 2026-10-16.2, and the follow-up marks both supporting rows Fixed.

Agent settings

One row, named "Claim tagger".

Who fills what: setup creates the row; a person ticks and clears Paused; the agent writes Rulebook edition and Last run summary.

Columns

ColumnTypeWho fills itMeaning
NametitlesetupThe row's name, Claim tagger.
Pausedcheckboxa personTicked by a person, every command then refuses; cleared by a person.
Rulebook editiontextthe agentThe edition in force: a date plus a count, such as 2026-10-16.1; it goes up when a rule changes.
Last run summarytextthe agentOne short line, such as "Promote · 16 Oct 11:20 · PASS".

Views

Every practice page uses the same four view names.

ViewTableRows shownSorted byColumns shown
Your queueTag decisionsTag outcome is emptyAgent confidence, lowest firstClaim, Agent proposal, Agent reason, Tag outcome, Why wrong, Your reasoning
Needs your noteTag decisionsWhy wrong is Rule unclear or Rule should change, and Your reasoning is emptyAgent confidence, lowest firstClaim, Tag outcome, Why wrong, Your reasoning
Lessons waitingRule changesStatus is Proposed or ApprovednoneLesson, Current text, Proposed text, Status; cells wrap, so both texts are read in place
RulebookRulebook copyall rowsnoneName, Category, Status, When to use, Example Claims; cells wrap

Words

  • Table: a Notion table of rows and columns; this page holds five.
  • Queue: the Tag decisions table: the answers the agent is unsure about, for the editor to decide; Your queue shows the ones that wait.
  • Rulebook: the numbered rules for each tag, kept in When to use in the Rulebook copy; it changes only after a safety check PASS or a restore.
  • Edition: the rulebook's version, a date plus a count (2026-10-16.1); it goes up when a rule changes.
  • Safety check: the test a rule change must pass before it is used: the example claims, the earlier decisions and the change's own rows (yours) must all come out right.
  • Practice page: a page under Demos where an editor runs the whole cycle once on sample claims, without touching anything real.
  • Agent proposal: the agent's answer for one claim and one tag: Applies, Does not apply or Can't tell.
  • Tag outcome: the editor's decision on a row; it always wins over the agent's answer.
  • Why wrong: the editor's reason: Agent slip (the rule is fine, no change), Rule unclear (the agent drafts a clearer rule), Rule should change (the agent drafts a changed rule).
  • Follow-up: after a PASS, the agent re-checks the rows the change rests on and marks each Fixed or Still wrong.

Open points: the relation columns of both copies are left out; the real claims table's six review columns are left out; only Context-dependent is judged, and the other twelve tags wait in the rulebook.
